memory_update.text: KRT is the highest-priority underfollowed public candidate for restaurant off-premise packaging because its public disclosures map directly to take-out containers, cups, lids, cutlery, compostable products, and restaurant/foodservice customers.
GPK is a mid-cap bridge candidate with QSR and foodservice cups/lids/containers exposure, but restaurant sensitivity must be separated from broader paperboard and CPG packaging exposure.

AMCR is a reference anchor rather than an underfollowed discovery candidate; its post-Berry scale may indicate consolidation and material-science advantages in foodservice packaging, but exposure purity is lower.

Major foodservice packaging assets such as Novolex/Pactiv Evergreen and Dart/Solo appear relevant to the node but are not currently clean US-listed equity candidates; monitor future IPO, spinoff, or supplier/customer disclosures.
Need to verify restaurant-channel revenue mix, QSR/customer concentration, compostable packaging margins, and regulatory-driven substrate shifts before promoting any candidate beyond Layer 1B.

node: Off-premise packaging, disposables, and delivery-enabling consumables
summary: Expanded the public-market universe for restaurant off-premise packaging with a two-lane funnel. The strongest underfollowed fit is Karat Packaging because its disclosed product set maps directly to take-out containers, cups, lids, cutlery, compostable products, and restaurant/foodservice customers. Graphic Packaging is a mid-cap reference-to-discovery bridge with QSR and foodservice cup/container exposure, but broader paperboard packaging makes restaurant sensitivity less pure. Amcor is a large-cap reference anchor after acquiring Berry Global, with foodservice called out as a growth category but diluted by global consumer and healthcare packaging. Reynolds Consumer Products is included as a weaker hypothesis because disposable tableware and foil/bakeware can benefit from takeout/catering behavior, but direct restaurant-channel exposure needs verification.
